newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Airbbus wins customers for new A340 models.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Airbbus wins customers for new A340 models.

text.p: A $2.5 billion gamble by European Airbus Industrie paid off on Friday when two high- profile airlines said they would order a new stretched model of its A340 long-range passenger jet.

In separate announcements, Britain's Virgin Atlantic Airways and Air Canada said they would be the launch customers for the A340-600 widebody jet, Airbus's challenge to Boeing Co's monopoly of the high-capacity segment.

Airbus Industrie managing director Jean Pierson announced the sales campaign for the 375-seat A340-600 and its longer- range derivative A340-500, at the Paris Air show in June. But unsually for a new product launch, Airbus had no launch customer committed to buy the aircraft.
Pierson said the development costs would be $2.5 billion for the two models.
"Getting a launch customer only one-and-a-half months after the commercial launch confirms the need for such a plane," an Airbus spokeswoman told Reuters.
The catalogue price for the A340-500 is $144 million and $158 million for the A340-600, she said.

The greater seating of the A340-600 brings Airbus within close-combat range of Boeing's 747, which seats around 400, and also rivals its modern 777 giant twinjet. Those two Boeing products enjoy high margins and give it the ability to cross- subsidise the range down to the smaller 737.
Virgin said it is acquiring 16 A340-600s, as well as two more A340-300 in a deal estimated by industry sources to be worth $2.5 billion.
Virgin plans to fit out the new A340-600 aircraft as two- deck aircraft with the lower deck featuring bedrooms for Upper Class passengers as well as showers, a bar and exercise and massage rooms.
"The layout will be stunning," said a spokesman for the airline.

Currently, Virgin operates 20 aircraft, including eight Airbus A340-300s, five Boeing 747-400s and an Airbus A320 narrow-body jet and six older generation 747s, which will be phased out with the arrival of the new aircraft.
A spokesman for Virgin said the airline will lease the aircraft, but declined to put a value on the order.
"All I can say is that we got a very good deal," he said.
Air Canada said it signed a letter of intent to acquire eight A330 and A340 aircraft from Airbus, with options for 20 additional aircraft.
The value of the eight aircraft, based on list prices, is about $1.4 billion, a news release issued by Air Canada said.

Air Canada is committing initially to ordering five A330-300 twinjets and three A340-300s. It has also set a March 1998 date to decide that if it expands its widebody fleet it will take five of the new 340-500 and 600 models.

The acquisition is part of the Canadian carrier's three- year programme to replace its widebody fleet with fuel- efficient and environmentally-friendly aircraft, reduce operating costs and provide passengers with state-of-the-art comfort, it said.
The new aircraft will replace its fleet of six Boeing 747-100/200 aircraft and two A340 aircraft currently under operating leases. Deliveries are scheduled to be completed by August 2000.
The A340-600 will have a range of 7,500 nautical miles, while the 500 version, which will fly 313 passengers up to 8,300 nautical miles, making it the longest range airliner in the world.
The new aircraft will be powered by a new version of Rolls-Royce Plc's Trent engines under a special development deal between the British engine maker and Airbus, which was also announced in June.

Current versions of the A340-200 and A340-300 seat, respectively, 261 and 295 passengers and fly up to 7,200 miles (13,300 km) and 7,300 miles (13,500 km). There is also an A340-8000, a development of the A340-200, which flies up to 8,000 miles.
Airbus is a consortium comprising French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) of Spain.
-- Pierre Tran, Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
